chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Bobby Moore, a holdup, and Bobby Carroll joins
summary: A holdup at a club, Moore's suicide, and Bobby Carroll joins and stays about ten years.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I heard about that. When you had Bobby Moore, was he still playing well, at the time you had him? He started losing his grip by that time.

He was getting a little flighty because we had a place--one night the place was held up and I noticed everybody was walking towards the back with their hands in the air, I didn't know what it was all about, and Bobby stood up with his trumpet, then I saw all these guns. He would have got us all killed; that was a hold up. The commissioner of police had just left there with his wife.
That was Commissioner Valentine?
Yes it was.
Bradon (phonetic spelling) didn't stay long with you, did he?
No, he committed suicide.
Did he commit suicide?
Yes. He found his wife with somebody and put his head in the oven and lit it.
So I had to get another trumpet player.
That's when I got Bobby Carroll.
He actually stayed with you as long as anybody?
He stayed with me about--
Nine, ten years or something like that.
Close to that.
The thing was he wasn't that reliable though; was he?
Yes he was. He liked to drink a lot but he was reliable.
That's what I'm saying, he was known to be such a heavy drinker.
Heavy drinker he was--
But he could still play?
He could still play, but

he liked--he would cause trouble and then when the band--I don't know, he was always jealous of the leader, but he always stuck, he never tried to leave. He would stir the guys up and then come over and get on my side.
Where is he from; do you know where he's from?
He's from Ohio.
I figured he must have come in the band right after Bobby Moore.
He came in the band--that's when, he followed Bobby Moore; you're right.
